name: Ashveil Splitback Recon Ghost Rig
description: Built for prolonged observation work in mid-density urban environments, this rig prioritizes stillness over movement — it's made to be worn for eight hours in a transit corridor, a market stall queue, or a service corridor without drawing a second look. The anchor piece is an anorak-style pullover in muted sand-ochre with subtle vertical stripe detail, a pattern common enough in Circuit-level workwear to register as background noise to any human observer or basic pattern-recognition surveillance. The anorak's hood is structured with internal wire framing that shapes to block facial recognition from above and side angles simultaneously, collapsing flat when not needed. A chest harness worn beneath the anorak — visible only when the zipper is opened — carries a modular tool rack: four interchangeable pouches that accept everything from a compact sidearm to a drone relay unit. The base layer is a long-sleeved thermal shirt in deep slate with a BCI-port collar notch at the rear nape, accommodating standard neural jack access without requiring the anorak to be removed. Trousers are straight-cut in medium grey with reinforced cuffs, an internal wire-routing sleeve along the right leg for aug-power, and three hidden waistband pockets accessible from inside the waistband only. Footwear is a low-profile athletic-style shoe in off-white with dark grey accent — the deliberate cleanliness of the shoes against the worn anorak reads as aspirational Tier 2, the universal human story of someone keeping one thing nice.
functionality: Structured facial-recognition-blocking hood, modular chest harness with four swappable pouches, BCI rear-nape port notch, aug-power routing right trouser leg, three internal waistband hidden pockets, prolonged-wear comfort construction
what_it_says: This outfit communicates patience. It isn't built for the sprint — it's built for the wait. The runner who wears this has spent enough time on observation jobs to understand that the greatest threat to a recon operative isn't being seen, it's being remembered. The clean shoes are the tell to anyone who knows how to look: deliberate detail management, not accident.
worn_by: runners who sell intelligence more than violence
manufacturer: Greymark Unseen — a near-anonymous street label that sells exclusively through dead-drop ordering systems; no storefront, no catalog, just reputation
story_hooks: The runner has been stationary for six hours in a transit corridor when the anorak's hood-wire frame begins to fatigue and reshape — the facial-geometry blocking degrades subtly, and an overhead drone's recognition confidence score climbs from 12% to 67% over the next forty minutes without the runner knowing.

The modular chest harness pouch system was loaded by a fixer's equipment runner, and one of the four pouches contains something the operative wasn't briefed on — something that explains why this particular surveillance contract pays three times the standard rate.

The BCI collar notch becomes a liability when a corponation security tech notices the specific cut during a pat-down inspection — it's a design tell unique to Greymark Unseen, and this particular security tech has a file on that label.

physical_description.visual_profile: A layered observation rig that reads as deliberately unremarkable — muted earth tones stacked for eight-hour surveillance endurance. The sand-ochre anorak dominates, its structured hood creating a subtle anonymity effect. Beneath, the slate thermal base and grey trousers form a neutral column. The outfit's genius is its invisibility: it registers as background-noise workwear to both human and machine vision, yet every element serves precision function.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed but intentional — the anorak hangs with enough volume to conceal the chest harness beneath, but the trousers sit clean and straight, avoiding both baggy and fitted extremes. The silhouette is designed for stillness: no excess fabric to telegraph movement, no compression that would restrict breathing during long static holds.
physical_description.primary_material: Anorak in treated synthetic-wool composite (stain-resistant, low-sheen). Base thermal in moisture-wicking synth-blend knit. Trousers in hardwearing cotton-poly reinforced at stress points. Shoes in recycled polymer mesh with elastomer sole.
physical_description.texture: Anorak has a matte, slightly weathered hand — subtle vertical ribbing catches light minimally. Thermal shirt is smooth, almost liquid against skin. Trouser fabric has a tight weave suggesting durability. Shoe uppers show deliberate cleanliness; sole treads are deep and utilitarian.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: sand-ochre anorak with muted vertical striping in taupe. Thermal base in deep slate grey. Trousers in medium grey. Shoes in off-white with dark charcoal accents. Overall palette is pre-dawn industrial — nothing that registers as chromatic noise to surveillance sweeps.
physical_description.closures: Anorak front-zip with magnetic snap-backs to prevent reflection glint. Hood drawcords blend into fabric (no hanging loose ends). Trousers have hidden magnetic waistband pockets. Shoes use friction-fit lacing system that won't catch on harness anchor points.
distinctive_features: Structured hood with internal wire framing — collapses to shape facial recognition angles from above and sides
Modular chest harness beneath anorak with four interchangeable quick-swap pouches (sidearm, relay unit, standard loadout compatible)
BCI-port collar notch at rear nape of thermal base — neural jack access without removing anorak
Internal wire-routing sleeve along right trouser leg for augmentation power lines
Three hidden waistband pockets accessible only from interior — defeats casual pickpocketing
Intentional wear pattern on anorak (subtle scuffs, faded hem) contrasts with pristine off-white shoes — signals aspirational Tier 2 authenticity
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2–3 boundary. The anorak and thermal suggest working-class functional, but the precision engineering and modular system design, plus the clean shoes, indicate someone with access to specialized gear. Price point is mid-tier contractor or security freelancer — enough Φ to afford purpose-built kit, not enough to show wealth.
physical_description.cultural_context: Street-side observer, surveillance professional, private security, investigative work. Wearing this says: 'I am trained to be invisible. I am equipped for extended static operations. I move through crowds without intention.' It reads as neither aggressive nor servile — just present, watching, waiting.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in but maintained. The anorak shows weathering and careful wear; the shoes stay pristine (a tell of someone who knows that footwear discipline prevents pattern recognition). Harness beneath stays hidden until revealed. Seams are tight, zippers function silently. No fraying, no loose threads — maintenance discipline.

image_prompt: A neo-noir recon operative in a sand-ochre anorak with structured hood half-raised, revealing the deep slate thermal base beneath. The hood frames the figure's face in shadow — geometric and deliberate. Chest harness visible where anorak zipper opens slightly, showing modular quick-swap pouches. Straight-cut grey trousers fade into off-white high-performance shoes that gleam with deliberate cleanliness. Figure stands motionless in a dimly lit transit corridor or market stall alcove — under harsh sodium vapor lighting and blue neon accent. The anorak's vertical striping catches light subtly, almost disappearing into background. Moody, surveillance-camera aesthetic. Dark concrete walls, distant crowd blur. The outfit reads as professional invisibility. Cinematic, low-contrast, industrial. --ar 2:3 --v 6
